That is almost it. Babies aren’t babbling because their mouth can’t make the correct sounds and this is what comes out. Babies babble because they can’t make the right sounds and they are practicing in order to build up those muscles. 

This is the same reason they start scribbling before they learn letter forms. However, the scribbling phase is often much longer because of how much later children learn letter forms, the scribbling often turns into children’s attempts to imitate prints. 

Furthermore, once children learn letterforms, they often approximate spelling based off of how words sound. This is actually great evidence for linguists to track pronunciation rules in different accents. On top of that, current research indicates that imaginary spelling like this is actually an important part of literary development and issues with it can even help diagnose dyslexia.
